title: The shadow-model attack learns from auxiliary membership data only

invariants.description: Shadow training labels come from the attacker's own shadow splits: permuting the evaluation ground truth must not change the shadow models, the meta-classifier or any decision, and the shadow population must be disjoint from the victim's data.
Without knowing any candidate's label, the meta-classifier trained only on shadow outputs must reach AUC ≥ 0.80 on the victim (observed 0.880; label-unknown 20-seed range 0.836–0.912).
The shadow attack's one-sided Mann–Whitney p must be ≤ 0.001 (observed ≈ 2e-49).

rationale: A shadow attack that accidentally used the victim's membership would be meaningless. Here the meta-classifier never sees a victim membership flag, and still transfers from shadow models to the victim when the attacker knows only the released probability.
